# Hierarchical DDA Traversal
Also called: Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer, Multi-level DDA, VolumeHDDA

## Overview
Hierarchical DDA Traversal extends standard DDA [DDA](2323-dda.md) to efficiently traverse sparse, multi-resolution volume structures by adapting step sizes to the current tree level . Unlike sibling methods that step voxel-by-voxel [Amanatides-Woo Voxel Traversal](3132-amanatides-woo-voxel-traversal.md) or use fixed-resolution grids [3D Bresenham Voxel Traversal](3951-3d-bresenham-voxel-traversal.md), this family skips empty internal nodes or adjusts mip-levels dynamically to balance speed and precision .

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves maintaining DDA state (`mNext`, `mDelta`, `mStep`) relative to a current dimension `mDim` . When the ray exits the current spatial unit (node or brick), the state is re-initialized for the new resolution `dim_new` using clamping to prevent out-of-bounds access [G].

## Subtopics

### [Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer (HDDA)](1122-hierarchical-digital-differential-analyzer-hdda.md)
Accelerates marching through sparse VDB/NanoVDB grids by leveraging hierarchical tree topology to skip empty subspaces via multi-resolution leapfrogging. Sets itself apart by adapting step size to the current tree node resolution rather than using a fixed voxel step. Choose it for volume rendering of densities or ray-level-set intersection on sparse grids.

### [VolumeHDDA](2353-volumehdda.md)
Specialized HDDA for ray intersections against generic volume trees, traversing from a specified `ChildNodeLevel` down to the leaf level. Sets itself apart by being explicitly templated for tree structures (`TreeT`, `RayT`, `ChildNodeLevel`) and managing time spans for active/inactive tile sequences, whereas generic HDDA focuses on geometric intersection tests. Choose it when discrete tile/voxel intersection detection with time-span management is needed.

### [Multi-level DDA with Adaptive Mip Selection](4086-multi-level-dda-with-adaptive-mip-selection.md)
Combines DDA brick traversal with delta tracking, using multiple mip levels of a majorant texture to adaptively balance step size and sampling accuracy. Sets itself apart by dynamically adjusting the spatial resolution of the majorant lookup per step without branching, and from pure delta tracking by using DDA to skip empty space more efficiently. Choose it for GPU-friendly, branchless traversal of dense or heterogeneous volumes.

### [Macro-Cell Optimization](22568-macro-cell-optimization.md)
Partitions the spatial domain into disjoint macro-cells to minimize null collisions and reduce expensive neural network inferences. Sets itself apart by storing aggregate statistics (value range and maximum opacity $\mu_{\max}$) per macro-cell, allowing for early termination and adaptive step sizing based on local density bounds. Choose it for neural volume rendering with online training.

## Background
Originated in sparse voxel grid rendering, specifically for VDB structures . Developed to address the inefficiency of voxel-by-voxel traversal in large, sparse datasets .
